plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-11 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Aviation Management program page and its linked official degree map, 'Aviation Management Degree Maps (2026-2027)', 'Aviation Management (Campus)' tab, last updated/reviewed August 3, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Collected as the BS: the program is a combined BA/BS, the catalog prints a single combined Total Credits, BA/BS Degree: 120, and the map expressly states that BA students take 16 credits of one foreign language, which are not included in the map; the BS version is recorded, following the prior-wave pattern for combined BA/BS programs. Every term's courses sum to the map's printed term total (16/14/15/15/15/15/15/15) and the plan to 120. The catalog prints the Aviation Management Curriculum as 50 credits (Aviation Core Requirements 16 + Aviation Electives 12 + Business Management Core Requirements 13 + Business Management Electives 9), and the map places exactly those blocks: all six Aviation Core courses, four 3-credit elective slots totalling the 12 Aviation Elective credits (the catalog's ten-course list is carried on the slots), all four Business Management Core courses, and three 3-credit elective slots totalling the 9 Business Management Elective credits (the catalog's nine-course list is carried on the slots; the catalog prints MGMT 3230 - Principles of Marketing, recorded as printed). The map notes that students also earn a minor in Management by completing this major. The map includes INFO 1010 Information Literacy (1 credit), which is not named in the catalog curriculum. Per the catalog, all courses must be passed with a C (2.0) or better to count in the major, and a maximum of 6 credits of aviation internship (AVTN 4890, or AVTN 2890 at the Chair's discretion) may be applied toward the degree in the general elective block. Catalog titles are recorded where the map shortens them.
